detail: The released miner exactly as downloaded. It only runs well with video memory at full speed, which costs about 35 W extra. Measured again after a 4-minute warm-up.
Same miner with the power-saving 810 MHz memory lock from miner.sh. It collapses because its matrices (about 670 MB) are far bigger than the GPU's cache.
Shrank the matrices to about 20 MB so they fit in the GPU's 32 MB cache. The GPU no longer waits on video memory. Short run on a cool card: steady-state power is about 10 W higher.

change: GPU code rebuilt with a newer compiler
detail: Recompiled the unchanged GPU code for RTX 50 cards with CUDA 13.5 instead of using the shipped build. Short run on a cool card: steady-state power is about 10 W higher.

Small matrices finish in under half a millisecond, so the GPU was idling while the CPU set up the next pass. Now 32 passes are queued at once. Short run on a cool card: steady-state power is about 10 W higher.

change: Matrix size matched to the 36 GPU cores
detail: Picked a size that divides evenly across the card's 36 compute cores, so none sit idle at the end of a pass. Short run on a cool card: steady-state power is about 10 W higher.

Rewrote the GPU kernel so the eight math threads issue their own data copies. Dropping the separate copy thread lifts a register limit and lets the fold step run without stalling. 590 test shares verified on the CPU. Short run on a cool card: steady-state power is about 10 W higher.

Same new kernel on the stock matrix size with memory unlocked. Fastest so far, but it runs into the 150 W power limit. Measured after a 4-minute warm-up: the card sits on the 150 W limit, which lowers the clock.

change: Whole batch in one kernel launch
detail: Noise generation and 128 passes now run inside a single GPU launch, so the cores no longer drain between passes. 776 test shares verified on the CPU. Measured after a 4-minute warm-up.
